hero.headline: House rejects resolution to remove troops from Lebanon
hero.body:
The House rejected a war powers resolution on Thursday that would have required President Trump to withdraw military forces from hostilities in Lebanon without congressional authorization. The chamber voted 324-92-2 against the measure, with significant Republican opposition.

Two hundred and seven Republicans and 117 Democrats voted to reject the resolution, along with one independent. Rep. Thomas Massie introduced the legislation seeking to limit the Trump administration's authority in Lebanon. The vote highlighted divisions within the Democratic Party, with party leadership opposing the effort.

War powers resolutions rely on the War Powers Act, a Vietnam War-era law that allows Congress to compel the president to remove armed forces from unauthorized hostilities abroad. The Constitution grants Congress the power to declare war, though presidents have frequently deployed troops without formal declarations or legislative approval.

The vote occurred as the United States maintains a military presence in Lebanon without explicit congressional authorization for military operations there. Those supporting the resolution argued that the deployment went beyond presidential authority. Opponents contended that the military engagement served national security interests and did not require additional approval from lawmakers.

The rejection of the measure leaves current deployments in place unchanged. This marks another instance in which Congress has declined to exercise its war powers authority to restrict presidential military action. The Trump administration has not publicly responded to the vote.

The outcome reflects broader patterns in Congress regarding war powers oversight. While some lawmakers have pushed back against military deployments, particularly those without prior authorization or formal declarations, Republicans have largely declined to impose checks on Trump through war powers votes.

The debate over the Lebanon resolution fits into a wider conversation about presidential power and military intervention that has intensified during Trump's second term. Democrats have attempted to force votes on multiple war powers resolutions as the administration has increased military activities in various regions and discussed potential military operations elsewhere.

Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the Lebanon measure, seeking to constrain executive authority in the region. Democratic leaders in the House opposed the resolution despite it being sponsored by a member of their party, signaling internal disagreement about how aggressively to challenge Trump on foreign policy matters.

The war powers votes reflect longstanding constitutional tensions over who controls military decisions. The Framers intended Congress to declare war and authorize military force, but modern presidents across parties have increasingly asserted independent authority to deploy troops. Congressional efforts to reclaim this power through war powers resolutions have met with limited success, particularly when one party controls the chamber.

The failed Lebanon resolution suggests that reasserting congressional war powers authority remains difficult in the current political environment, despite growing concerns among some lawmakers about military expansion overseas.

cards.headline: Zelensky Proposes Direct Talks With Putin to End War
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president sent an open letter to Russia's leader calling for face-to-face negotiations.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has proposed direct face-to-face negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in an open letter, arguing that only bilateral engagement between the two countries can resolve the conflict. Zelensky called for a full ceasefire and suggested meeting in a neutral country to restart peace discussions.

The proposal comes as diplomatic efforts around the Ukraine conflict remain fragmented. The EU has grown concerned about being sidelined from substantive negotiations, with European leaders increasingly worried that discussions between the US, Russia, and Ukraine have stalled while leaving the bloc vulnerable to accepting a deal it does not support. European capitals have long insisted that any talks affecting Ukraine must include Kyiv's participation.

Russia has continued to set preconditions for negotiations. The Kremlin demands that Ukraine withdraw its troops from the eastern Donbas region before serious talks can begin. Putin's advisers have indicated that he remains determined to seize remaining parts of the region by force this year before any meaningful discussions commence.

Ukraine has flatly rejected any suggestion that it would unilaterally withdraw from its own territory. This position has been strengthened by recent developments on the battlefield, where Russian advances have largely stalled. Both armies show mounting signs of exhaustion and continue to sustain heavy casualties while conducting strikes against each other's energy infrastructure.

The conflict shows few signs of diplomatic resolution. Analysts assess that a breakthrough remains unlikely given the current military stalemate and entrenched positions of both sides. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius has suggested that Putin's recent peace remarks may be a tactical maneuver rather than a genuine move toward ending the war. "If he sees the end of this war approaching, couldn't he simply end it himself?" Pistorius said during a visit to Kyiv, suggesting that Putin's conditions indicate continued deception rather than serious intent to negotiate.

The diplomatic landscape has also been complicated by disputes over who should represent various parties in peace talks. The EU rejected Putin's suggestion that Gerhard Schröder, a former German chancellor with longstanding ties to Moscow, serve as a European mediator. EU top diplomat Kaja Kallas stated that allowing Russia to appoint a negotiator for Europe would be unwise, noting that Schröder's past work as a high-level lobbyist for Russian state-owned companies, including Nord Stream gas pipelines and Rosneft, made him unsuitable. "It is clear why Putin wants him to be the person, so that actually he would be sitting on both sides of the table," Kallas said.

A US-brokered ceasefire was scheduled to expire, with Moscow rejecting efforts to extend the truce. The path toward resolving the more than four-year conflict remains uncertain as all parties maintain competing demands and strategic positions.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects Cease-Fire Deal Between Lebanon and Israel
cards.teaser: Hezbollah rejected a cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon brokered by the United States, with the group's leader saying the terms amounted to surrend.
cards.body:
The United States announced a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon on Wednesday night following fresh negotiations. Hezbollah, which was excluded from the U.S.-brokered talks, rejected the deal. The Iran-backed group's leader characterized the agreement as surrender, arguing that any truce negotiated without their participation does not reflect the situation on the ground.

The breakdown of the ceasefire effort highlights the difficulty in securing a lasting halt to hostilities along the Israel-Lebanon border. The agreement involved Israeli and Lebanese government officials but excluded Hezbollah, a significant military force in southern Lebanon that has been engaged in periodic fighting with Israeli forces. A U.N. peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon during this period of tension.

cards.headline: Former National Security Advisor John Bolton to plead guilty in classified documents case
cards.teaser: John Bolton has reached a deal to plead guilty to charges related to mishandling classified information.
cards.body:
Former National Security Advisor John Bolton has reached a plea agreement in a classified documents case. Under the deal, which is subject to court approval, Bolton will plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information.

Bolton served as national security advisor under President Trump from April 2018 to September 2019. He later became a vocal critic of the administration and published a memoir about his time in office that raised concerns over classified material handling.

cards.headline: Trump says he will nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump announced plans to nominate his acting attorney general Todd Blanche to lead the Justice Department permanently.
cards.body:
President Trump has announced his intention to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general. Blanche is currently serving as acting attorney general. If confirmed by the Senate, Trump's former personal lawyer would become the administration's top prosecutor at the Department of Justice.

The nomination will require Senate confirmation. Senator John Fetterman has indicated he will vote against Blanche's confirmation.

cards.headline: Dow Jones Surges Nearly 900 Points to Record Close as Investors Exit Tech Stocks
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high with gains approaching 900 points as market participants moved capital out of technology stocks.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged nearly 900 points to reach a record close as investors rotated away from technology stocks. The S&P 500 also gained ground during the session, with financials leading the advance.

Semiconductor shares declined during the trading day, with chip stocks including Broadcom, Micron, and ARM moving lower. This shift reflected a broader rotation away from artificial intelligence-related names, even as the overall market demonstrated strength across other sectors.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans narrowly defeat effort to block Trump's $1.8 billion ally payment fund
cards.teaser: The Senate rejected multiple amendments aimed at eliminating a fund Trump plans to use to pay allies.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans on Thursday blocked a Democratic effort to prevent President Trump from creating a $1.8 billion fund to pay his allies. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer had proposed adding language to Republican-backed deportation legislation that would bar the payouts, but the measure narrowly failed.

The vote exposed divisions within the GOP, with three Republican senators joining Democrats in opposing the fund. The dispute centers on what critics have called an "anti-weaponization" program, even as signs emerged of spreading dissent among Trump's own party over the proposal.

cards.headline: Armed Clashes Erupt in Mogadishu
cards.teaser: Gun battles between rival political factions broke out in Somalia's capital in the worst fighting in years.
cards.body:
Fierce fighting broke out between government troops and opposition-allied militias in Mogadishu on Wednesday afternoon. The violence forced civilians to flee and caused significant property damage, with residents describing it as the worst fighting the capital has experienced in years.

The clashes occurred as opposition leaders embedded with militias established positions in their clan strongholds throughout the city. The fighting erupted ahead of planned protests over the president's decision to remain in office after his term expired.

cards.headline: Ultra-Orthodox Israelis Riot Over Military Draft
cards.teaser: Violent protests by Haredi communities against mandatory military service have escalated ahead of national elections.
cards.body:
Israel's ultra-Orthodox community has intensified protests against military conscription in recent weeks, with the latest demonstrations turning violent. The riots have shocked many Israelis and highlighted deepening social divisions within the country.

The Haredi community has traditionally been exempt from military service, but efforts to expand the draft have met with fierce resistance. The escalating protests come as Israel prepares for national elections, with the issue of military service becoming a focal point of political debate.

cards.headline: Former Trump Advisor John Bolton to Plead Guilty in Documents Case
cards.teaser: The former national security advisor reached a deal with prosecutors over classified materials.
cards.body:
John Bolton, former national security adviser under President Trump and later a vocal critic of the administration, has reached a plea agreement in a classified documents case. According to a source familiar with the matter, Bolton will plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information, subject to court approval.

The Justice Department filed charges against Bolton in 2025. Bolton departed Trump's first administration and subsequently wrote a critical memoir of his time in office.

cards.headline: Ex-Wife of Dubai Ruler's Nephew in Custody
cards.teaser: Zeynab Javadli has not contacted friends since Tuesday, prosecutors say.
cards.body: Zeynab Javadli, the former wife of Dubai's ruler's nephew, has been taken into custody, prosecutors confirmed. Her lawyer, British legal representative David Haigh, reported losing contact with her on Tuesday. When checked, her Dubai home was found locked and empty. The case has attracted attention due to Javadli's former ties to the Dubai ruling family.

cards.headline: Nose Gear Collapses on Lufthansa Dreamliner at Frankfurt Airport
cards.teaser: Several workers were injured when a Boeing 787-9 collapsed during ground operations.
cards.body:
The nose gear on a Lufthansa Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner collapsed at Frankfurt Airport, injuring several workers. The airline said the cause of the accident is under investigation.

The aircraft can weigh up to 279 tons at takeoff. The collapse occurred during ground operations, though the specific circumstances that led to the gear failure have not been determined. The incident adds to ongoing scrutiny of Boeing aircraft safety.

hero.headline: Public health departments lose enforcement powers following pandemic backlash
hero.body:
Public health authorities across the United States have seen their powers curtailed as state and local governments respond to criticism of measures taken during the COVID-19 pandemic. The changes affect the ability of health departments to impose lockdowns, mandate masks, require vaccinations, and close schools during disease outbreaks.

The rollback comes after widespread public pushback against restrictions implemented to control the spread of COVID-19. Many jurisdictions have revised laws and regulations that previously granted broad emergency powers to public health officials. The changes vary by location but collectively represent a significant shift in how local and state governments can respond to infectious disease threats.

Public health experts warn that the weakened authorities could increase risks during future outbreaks. The ability to act quickly during health emergencies has traditionally been considered a core function of public health departments. Restrictions on these powers may slow response times when new infectious diseases emerge or existing diseases spread rapidly through communities.

The debate reflects ongoing tensions between individual liberty and collective public health measures. Critics of pandemic-era restrictions argued that lockdowns and mandates caused economic damage, disrupted education, and infringed on personal freedoms. Supporters of strong public health powers contend that such measures save lives during outbreaks and that elected officials should defer to health experts during medical emergencies.

The legal changes create a patchwork of public health authority across the country. Some jurisdictions now require legislative approval for measures that health officials could previously implement independently. Others have placed time limits on emergency declarations or restricted the types of interventions health departments can mandate. These variations mean that neighboring communities may have vastly different capacities to respond to the same health threat.

cards.teaser: John Bolton has reached a deal to plead guilty to charges related to mishandling classified information.

Former National Security Advisor John Bolton has reached a plea agreement in a classified documents case. Under the deal, which is subject to court approval, Bolton will plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information.

cards.headline: Jury views evidence in murder trial over fatal stabbing at Texas high school track meet
cards.teaser: Jurors in the Karmelo Anthony trial saw surveillance footage as prosecutors argue the killing was murder, not self-defense.
cards.body:
The trial of Karmelo Anthony continued with prosecutors presenting evidence that Anthony murdered Austin Metcalf at a Frisco ISD track meet. The prosecution told jurors the killing was not an act of self-defense, and presented claims that Anthony taunted Metcalf before the stabbing.

Jury selection in the case faced complications when questions about immigration status sparked pushback. Surveillance video from the track meet was shown to jurors as part of the prosecution's case. The trial is taking place in Texas.

cards.headline: United jet was too slow and too low before Newark landing accident, investigators say
cards.teaser: A United 767 from Italy struck a light pole while landing at Newark, damaging a truck on the turnpike below.
cards.body:
Federal investigators determined that the captain of a United Airlines Boeing 767 was flying too slowly and at an insufficient altitude during the approach to Newark Liberty International Airport last month. The aircraft was arriving from Italy when the incident occurred.

During the landing, the jet struck a light pole, which caused damage to a truck on the New Jersey Turnpike below. The NTSB's investigation focused on the pilot's actions and decisions that led to these conditions during the approach and landing.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center begins removing Trump name following court ruling
cards.teaser: Staff at the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts received a memo directing them to remove references to Trump's name.
cards.body:
The Kennedy Center has instructed staff to begin removing President Trump's name from the arts center following a judicial ruling that the name was illegally added. An internal memo directed employees to remove Trump references from documents and materials immediately.

The removal process extends beyond the Kennedy Center, with Trump's name disappearing from other institutions as well. A federal judge previously determined that adding Trump's name to the Kennedy Center violated legal requirements.

cards.headline: Trump says he will nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump announced plans to nominate his acting attorney general Todd Blanche to lead the Justice Department permanently.
cards.body:
President Trump has announced his intention to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general. Blanche is currently serving as acting attorney general. If confirmed by the Senate, Trump's former personal lawyer would become the administration's top prosecutor at the Department of Justice.

The vote exposed divisions within the GOP, with three Republican senators joining Democrats in opposing the fund. The dispute centers on what critics have called an "anti-weaponization" program, even as signs emerged of spreading dissent among Trump's own party over the proposal.

hero.headline: Wall Street Banks Prepare for Largest IPO Ever with SpaceX Offering
hero.body:
Elon Musk's SpaceX is moving forward with plans to become a publicly traded company, enlisting major Wall Street banks to manage what could become the largest initial public offering in history. Four leading financial institutions—JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley—are in discussions to lead the offering.

The aerospace company is targeting a massive capital raise, with reports indicating SpaceX could seek up to $75 billion from the public markets. This valuation would give the company a market value of approximately $1.77 trillion, according to recent reporting. Such a scale underscores the significance of the transaction and explains why senior Wall Street executives are personally involved in the pitch process.

SpaceX has grown into a dominant force in commercial spaceflight over the past two decades. The company operates a fleet of reusable rockets that launch satellites, conduct government contracts with NASA, and resupply the International Space Station. Beyond its core aerospace business, SpaceX also manages Starlink, a satellite internet service that has deployed thousands of satellites and serves customers across dozens of countries worldwide.

The company's financial performance supports its enormous valuation. SpaceX reported annual revenues of $15.5 billion, with approximately $1.1 billion coming from NASA contracts. Recent private funding rounds valued the business at between $400 billion and $800 billion before this public offering.

The decision to go public represents a notable shift for Musk, who has previously expressed concerns about operating companies in public markets due to investor scrutiny and short-term pressure. SpaceX has remained private since its founding, relying on private capital raises to fuel its expansion and ambitious projects.

The timing aligns with broader expectations of significant technology sector IPOs in coming months. Other high-profile companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are also reportedly considering public listings, with valuations reaching into the hundreds of billions and trillions of dollars. Industry analysts refer to these mega-valued startups as "hectocorns" due to their valuations exceeding $100 billion.

For Wall Street banks, the SpaceX transaction represents extraordinary fee potential. Investment banks typically earn a percentage of capital raised in IPOs, meaning a $75 billion offering would generate substantial revenue for the managing institutions.

According to one analyst, while Musk's Mars colonization ambitions capture headlines, investors will focus on more concrete growth plans. These include expanding infrastructure such as solar farms and data centers in orbit, which could diversify SpaceX's revenue streams beyond traditional launch services.

The SpaceX IPO will serve as a bellwether for the broader technology sector, testing whether investor enthusiasm for transformative companies can sustain valuations in the trillions of dollars.

cards.headline: Dow Jones Surges Nearly 900 Points to Record Close as Investors Exit Tech Stocks
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high with gains approaching 900 points as market participants moved capital out of technology stocks.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged nearly 900 points to reach a record close as investors rotated away from technology stocks. The S&P 500 also gained ground during the session, with financials leading the advance.

Semiconductor shares declined during the trading day, with chip stocks including Broadcom, Micron, and ARM moving lower. This shift reflected a broader rotation away from artificial intelligence-related names, even as the overall market demonstrated strength across other sectors.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Drops to Pre-Iran Conflict Levels as Cryptocurrency Decline Continues
cards.teaser: Bitcoin has fallen to prices last seen before the Iran conflict began, extending a decline that marks its worst week in months.
cards.body:
Bitcoin fell to levels not seen since before the Iran conflict, continuing a slide that represents its ugliest week in recent months. The cryptocurrency has declined as market narratives that previously supported prices have faded and investment capital has rotated to other assets.

Strategy's Michael Saylor attributed Bitcoin's decline to competition from artificial intelligence stocks. The cryptocurrency's sagging price has prompted some market observers to declare victory for bears, though others maintain it is premature to rule out a recovery.

cards.headline: Quantinuum Stock Closes Flat After Raising $1.68 Billion in Quantum Computing IPO
cards.teaser: Quantinuum's stock closed flat in its Nasdaq debut after the quantum computing company raised $1.68 billion in an upsized initial public offering.
cards.body:
Quantinuum made its Nasdaq debut after raising $1.68 billion through an upsized initial public offering. The quantum computing company, backed by Honeywell, saw its stock close flat on its first trading day despite investor enthusiasm that led to an expansion of the original offering size.

The flat close reflected market volatility during the highly anticipated debut. The IPO marked a significant milestone for the quantum computing sector as it moves toward broader public market participation.

cards.headline: Lululemon Cuts Annual Forecast After Disappointing Product Launches
cards.teaser: Lululemon reduced its annual revenue forecast, citing negative media coverage and disappointing product launches as pressures mount before a new CEO takes over.
cards.body:
Lululemon cut its annual revenue outlook after citing negative media commentary and disappointing product launches. The athletic apparel retailer trimmed its forecast for the fiscal year, adding pressure ahead of the arrival of a new chief executive.

The company acknowledged that far more work is needed to achieve a turnaround. Shares of Lululemon sank following the announcement of the revised guidance for fiscal 2026, with the stock declining as investors processed the reduced expectations for the retailer's performance.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Backs Trump Administration on Telecom Regulation Authority
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court sided with the Trump administration in a case concerning federal authority to regulate telecommunications companies.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 in favor of the Federal Communications Commission's authority to impose fines on wireless carriers through in-house proceedings. AT&T and Verizon had challenged the system, arguing it violated their constitutional right to a jury trial. The decision upheld the FCC's penalty system and handed a win to the Trump administration.

The ruling settles a dispute over the scope of the FCC's regulatory power in the telecom sector, affirming the agency's ability to conduct its own enforcement proceedings without jury involvement.

cards.headline: Netflix Shifts to Fewer Films Under New Movie Strategy
cards.teaser: Netflix is producing fewer movies under a new strategy led by executive Dan Lin, who still greenlights more films than any other studio.
cards.body:
Netflix has adopted a new approach to film production focused on making fewer but higher-quality movies. The strategy is being implemented by Dan Lin, who does not cater to stars or approve unlimited budgets.

Despite the reduction in total output, Lin continues to greenlight more films than any other single executive in the industry. The shift represents a change in how the streaming service approaches its movie slate, prioritizing quality over volume in its content decisions.

hero.headline: Fusion startup Helion raises $465 million to build Microsoft power plant
hero.body:
Helion, a fusion energy company backed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, has secured $465 million in funding to construct a power plant for Microsoft. The startup is working toward completing the facility by 2028 as part of an agreement with the technology company.

Fusion energy operates by combining atomic nuclei to produce large amounts of power, replicating the process that fuels the sun. This differs from conventional nuclear fission, which splits atoms. Fusion generates significantly less radioactive waste and carries lower safety risks compared to traditional nuclear energy. Helion is developing technology that uses pulsed magnetic fields to compress and heat plasma to the temperatures needed for fusion reactions.

The new funding will support construction of the power plant designed to supply electricity directly to Microsoft. The 2028 target represents an ambitious deadline within an industry where commercial fusion power has consistently remained distant despite decades of research and substantial investment. Several fusion companies have attracted billions in venture capital recently, wagering that progress in materials science, magnet technology, and computing power will enable the technology to become commercially practical.

As part of its strategy to meet increasing energy demands from data centers and artificial intelligence systems, Microsoft has committed to purchasing electricity from the Helion facility. Large technology companies have increasingly explored alternative energy sources, including small modular nuclear reactors and enhanced geothermal systems, to power growing infrastructure while advancing carbon reduction targets.

While Helion previously announced its partnership with Microsoft, the company had not revealed the financial details necessary for plant construction. The $465 million funding round ranks among the largest in the fusion sector, demonstrating investor confidence in both Helion's technical method and its capacity to achieve the Microsoft deadline.

The broader context for this investment reflects significant recent activity in fusion energy development. Multiple major technology companies and AI leaders have begun investing heavily in fusion startups. This surge in interest stems from growing electricity demands from artificial intelligence and data centers, creating pressure on power grids worldwide.

Whether Helion successfully meets its 2028 timeline will likely influence how investors view fusion energy's potential as a near-term power solution. The company joins other fusion developers working to transition the technology from experimental phases to commercial operations. Success or failure at this stage could shape the trajectory of investment and development across the entire fusion sector.

cards.headline: Filtr blocks ads in iPhone and Mac apps using new Apple software feature
cards.teaser: An ad blocker app now stops ads from loading inside apps on Apple devices.
cards.body:
Filtr is an ad blocking app for iPhones, iPads, and Macs that now blocks advertisements from loading inside apps, including web browsers. The expanded capability is powered by a new feature in the latest Apple software.

The app leverages this new Apple feature to provide system-wide ad blocking across a broader range of applications on Apple devices, rather than being limited to blocking ads in specific contexts or individual apps.

cards.headline: Apple approves first AI agent for Messages for Business platform
cards.teaser: Poke became the first AI agent approved to operate on Apple's business messaging system.
cards.body:
Poke has become the first AI agent approved to operate on Apple's Messages for Business platform. The startup enables users to interact with AI agents directly through text messages on Apple devices.

Apple's Messages for Business platform allows companies to communicate with customers through the Messages app. This approval represents a significant expansion of Apple's ecosystem, opening the platform to third-party AI services for the first time.

cards.headline: Severe geomagnetic storm could bring northern lights to 25 states
cards.teaser: A solar storm heading toward Earth may make auroras visible across much of the northern United States.
cards.body:
A geomagnetic storm upgraded to G3 severity is expected to reach Earth, potentially making the northern lights visible in 25 states. The storm watch covers the period from June 4 to June 5.

The forecast includes states across the northern tier of the country, with visibility expected in Vermont, New York, New Hampshire, and southeast Michigan. G3-class storms are considered strong and can cause auroras to appear at lower latitudes than usual.

cards.headline: Meta builds data centers in tents to cut costs
cards.teaser: The company adopted tent structures for data centers, borrowing a tactic previously used by Tesla.
cards.body:
Meta is constructing data centers using tent structures as a way to reduce its infrastructure expenses. The approach mirrors a strategy Tesla has used for some of its operations.

Data centers represent a significant capital expense for Meta, housing the servers and equipment needed to run its social media platforms and artificial intelligence systems. The tent-based construction method may offer faster deployment and lower building costs compared to traditional data center facilities.

cards.headline: Google launches customizable search result pages for creators and publishers
cards.teaser: Social media personalities and publishers can now personalize how their content appears in Google search.
cards.body:
Google introduced Search Profiles, a new feature that lets content creators and publishers customize how they appear in Google search results. The profiles provide creators with an official presence directly within the search system to showcase their work.

The move addresses concerns about how AI-generated summaries in search results have reduced traffic to original content sources. By offering customizable profiles, Google gives creators a dedicated way to highlight their work and connect with audiences searching on the platform.

cards.headline: Elon Musk challenges FTC oversight of X data handling
cards.teaser: The X owner is attempting to stop Federal Trade Commission audits of the platform's privacy practices.
cards.body:
Elon Musk filed to escape FTC audits of how X handles user data. Public commenters responding to the request warned the FTC that Musk cannot be trusted to protect user privacy on the platform.

The FTC has maintained oversight of Twitter, now called X, following previous consent agreements related to data privacy. Musk's attempt to end the audits represents his latest effort to reduce regulatory scrutiny of the social media company.

hero.headline: Packers sign Christian Watson to four-year, $110.5 million extension
hero.body:
The Green Bay Packers and wide receiver Christian Watson reached agreement Thursday on a four-year contract extension worth $110.5 million, sources confirmed to ESPN. The deal includes a $31 million signing bonus.

Watson, who was drafted by Green Bay in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft, has emerged as a key weapon in the Packers offense. The extension secures his services through the 2029 season and represents one of the larger wide receiver contracts in the league.

The $110.5 million total value places Watson among the higher-paid receivers in professional football. The $31 million signing bonus provides immediate financial security while spreading the salary cap impact across multiple years. The four-year structure gives the Packers cost certainty at the position through the end of the decade.

The timing of the extension comes as teams across the league have been investing heavily in the wide receiver position. Watson's deal follows a trend of organizations locking up young offensive talent to long-term contracts before they reach free agency. The Packers have now committed significant resources to their passing game infrastructure.

Green Bay will enter the upcoming season with Watson under contract as a cornerstone of their receiving corps. The extension removes any potential contract uncertainty and allows both the player and organization to focus on on-field performance.

cards.headline: Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin requests trade
cards.teaser: The Detroit captain has asked the organization to move him, sources confirmed Thursday.
cards.body:
Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin has requested a trade from the organization, sources told ESPN on Thursday. The request marks a significant development for the franchise and its longest-tenured star player.

Larkin has been with Detroit since being drafted in 2014 and was named team captain in 2021. The trade request creates uncertainty around the Red Wings roster as the organization enters the offseason. Detroit will now need to evaluate trade options and determine the next steps for their leadership group.

cards.headline: Liverpool appoint Andoni Iraola as new head coach
cards.teaser: The Premier League club confirmed Iraola will replace Arne Slot as manager.
cards.body:
Liverpool have confirmed the appointment of Andoni Iraola as their new head coach on a two-year contract. The 43-year-old Spaniard replaces Arne Slot, who was sacked just six days before Iraola's announcement.

Iraola joins Liverpool after spells at Bournemouth, Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace. The club moved quickly to secure their preferred candidate, identifying him as ideal for their tactical vision. Iraola previously worked with Liverpool's technical director Richard Hughes during his time at Bournemouth.

cards.headline: Two fans receive lifetime NBA bans after Finals selfie incident
cards.teaser: The league handed down permanent arena bans following a selfie-seeking incident during Game 1.
cards.body:
Two fans have received lifetime bans from all NBA arenas following an incident during Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday night. A man ran onto the court to take a selfie with San Antonio Spurs player Victor Wembanyama, prompting the league's swift disciplinary action announced Thursday.

The NBA is also investigating a separate incident from the same game involving Knicks star Jalen Brunson, who became upset during an interaction with courtside fans in the fourth quarter. The Knicks defeated the Spurs 105-95 in the Finals opener.

cards.headline: NBA investigating Jalen Brunson interaction with courtside fans
cards.teaser: The league is reviewing an incident between the Knicks star and fans late in Game 1 of the Finals.
cards.body:
The NBA is investigating an interaction between Knicks star Jalen Brunson and courtside fans during the fourth quarter of Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday night at Madison Square Garden. Brunson appeared upset following the exchange with fans during New York's 105-95 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.

The investigation comes as the league also addressed a separate incident in which two fans received lifetime bans from all NBA arenas after running onto the court to take a selfie with Spurs player Victor Wembanyama during the same game.

cards.headline: Aaron Judge misses third straight game with rib injury
cards.teaser: The Yankees slugger sat out Thursday as the team awaits medical clarity on a bone bruise.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge was out of the lineup Thursday for a third straight game as the Yankees await clarity about a bone bruise in one of his right ribs that is causing right shoulder pain. The outfielder has been sidelined since the injury was diagnosed earlier this week.

The bone bruise has created cascading effects that have kept Judge from playing. New York is proceeding cautiously with their star player as they gather more medical information about the injury and its impact on his shoulder. The team has not provided a timeline for his return to action.

cards.headline: Golden Knights lead Hurricanes 1-0 in Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: Vegas took the series opener as the NHL championship continues.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights hold a 1-0 series lead over the Carolina Hurricanes in the Stanley Cup Final after winning the opening game. The series continues as both teams compete for the championship.

Vegas gained the early advantage in the best-of-seven series with their Game 1 victory. The Hurricanes will look to even the series in the next contest. The Stanley Cup Final represents the culmination of the NHL playoffs, with both teams seeking their first championship of the season.

hero.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
hero.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian artist and graphic novelist whose acclaimed memoir Persepolis reshaped international understanding of Iran, has died at age 56. Her family stated that she "died of sadness" following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, who passed away on April 8, 2023. Later that month, messages posted on Satrapi's Instagram account included the phrase: "For I lost the love of my life."

Born in 1969 in Rasht, Iran, Satrapi grew up in Tehran with her father, an engineer, and her mother, a dress designer. As a teenager, her parents sent her to Europe to continue her education and escape the restrictions of the Islamic Republic. She eventually settled in France in 1994 and became a French citizen in 2006.

Satrapi published Persepolis in 2000, a four-volume graphic memoir that became an international publishing success. The work chronicled her childhood during Iran's 1979 revolution and the subsequent Iran-Iraq War, following a rebellious young girl as she navigated the country's violence and ideological control before being sent alone to Europe at age 14. The memoir sold millions of copies and established Satrapi as one of the most widely read Iranian authors globally. She initially had modest expectations for the project, telling El País in 2020: "With Persepolis, I didn't even think I'd find a publisher. I thought I'd make 50 photocopies for my friends to read."

Satrapi co-directed the animated film adaptation of Persepolis, which became an international success. She made history as the first woman nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. She later directed five feature films, including Radioactive in 2019, starring Rosamund Pike as physicist Marie Curie.

Regarding her choice of medium, Satrapi said: "Drawing it's the first language of human beings, before writing, before even talking, before words." She described the purpose of her work as reassuring young Iranians they were heard and supported globally, stating: "If they kill you and the whole world doesn't care, how is that? This is the whole thing I'm asking: just recognise this."

In 2024, Satrapi returned to comics by coordinating Woman, Life, Freedom, a collaborative graphic work featuring 17 Iranian and international comic artists alongside academics. The book examined protests following the 2022 death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish-Iranian woman detained for allegedly failing to comply with mandatory headscarf rules. Discussing the project, Satrapi said: "The only thing I can do is cultural work. This book is a message to the Iranian people to say, listen, you are not alone."

Her death prompted tributes from French political leaders and international figures. President Emmanuel Macron called her "a great artist who turned her Iranian childhood into a universal tale." Margaret Atwood noted that Satrapi "lived" experiences of repression that Atwood had only written about, describing her work as increasingly pertinent given Iran's current circumstances.

cards.headline: Starz Greenlights Power: Legacy Starring Joseph Sikora and Michael Rainey Jr.
cards.teaser: The network has ordered eight episodes of the latest Power franchise sequel, reuniting characters from previous series.
cards.body:
Starz has ordered Power: Legacy to series, bringing together Tommy Egan and Tariq St. Patrick in a new chapter of the long-running franchise. Joseph Sikora and Michael Rainey Jr. will reprise their roles, with the series following the reunion of Tommy and Tariq, son of Tommy's late friend James Ghost St. Patrick.

The network committed to eight episodes for the first season. Both actors previously led their own Power spinoff series, with Sikora starring in Power Book IV: Force and Rainey heading Power Book II: Ghost. The new series marks another expansion of the Power universe, which began with the original series in 2014.

cards.headline: Producer Sues Amazon and Vice Studios Over Hollywood Hustler Documentary
cards.teaser: Julio Hallivis alleges the documentary falsely portrayed him as an accomplice to convicted fraudster Zach Horwitz.
cards.body:
Producer Julio Hallivis filed a defamation lawsuit against Amazon Studios, Vice Studios, and director Rebecca Chaiklin on Thursday over the documentary series Hollywood Hustler: Glitz, Glam, Scam. The series examined the case of convicted fraudster Zach Horwitz.

Hallivis claims the documentary falsely portrayed him as an accomplice in Horwitz's fraud scheme, damaging his professional reputation in the entertainment industry. The lawsuit seeks damages from the production companies and streaming platform.

cards.headline: YouTuber Jesse Ridgway and Wife Discuss Decision to Terminate Pregnancy After Down Syndrome Diagnosis
cards.teaser: The influencer couple shared their experience with followers, drawing significant public reaction.
cards.body:
YouTube personality Jesse Ridgway and his wife disclosed that they terminated a pregnancy after receiving a fetal Down syndrome diagnosis. The couple discussed what they described as a difficult choice in content shared with their online audience.

The announcement generated substantial backlash across social media platforms. The couple's decision to publicly share their experience sparked widespread debate among their followers and the broader online community about pregnancy decisions and disability.

cards.headline: 60 Minutes Executive Producer Pledges Editorial Independence as CBS Awaits Correspondent Decisions
cards.teaser: The new leader addressed staff concerns about editorial control while uncertainty remains over key personnel.
cards.body:
The new executive producer of 60 Minutes sent a memo to staff Thursday affirming the program's commitment to pursue stories without fear or favor. The statement comes as the program faces significant turnover, with three of its seven full-time correspondents recently fired and another departing.

Fired correspondent Scott Pelley accused CBS News executives of instructing him to inject falsehoods and bias into reporting. The departures of Pelley, Sharyn Alfonsi, and Cecilia Vega, along with Anderson Cooper's February exit, have raised questions about who will staff the show's 59th season beginning in September and whether it will maintain its identity.

cards.headline: Dateline Examines Luigi Mangione Case in Friday Special
cards.teaser: The NBC program explores the investigation into Mangione, describing him as a figure people use as a Rorschach test.
cards.body:
Dateline will air a special investigation into Luigi Mangione on Friday, June 5, at 10 p.m. ET. The program will examine the case surrounding Mangione, with producers characterizing him as someone the public has used as a projection of their own interpretations.

The special represents the news program's deeper examination of the investigation. NBC has scheduled the episode as part of its ongoing true crime coverage, exploring how the case has captured public attention and generated varied reactions.

cards.headline: Seeker Music Acquires Cocteau Twins Member Simon Raymonde's Publishing Catalog
cards.teaser: The deal includes Raymonde's work with the influential band and his solo projects.
cards.body:
Evan Bogart's Seeker Music has acquired the music publishing catalog of Simon Raymonde, longtime member of Cocteau Twins. The catalog encompasses his work as a songwriter, producer, and instrumentalist with the influential Scottish band.

hero.headline: House rejects resolution to remove troops from Lebanon
hero.body:
The House rejected a war powers resolution on Thursday that would have required President Trump to withdraw military forces from hostilities in Lebanon without congressional authorization. The chamber voted 324-92-2 against the measure, with significant Republican opposition.

Two hundred and seven Republicans and 117 Democrats voted to reject the resolution, along with one independent. Rep. Thomas Massie introduced the legislation seeking to limit the Trump administration's authority in Lebanon. The vote highlighted divisions within the Democratic Party, with party leadership opposing the effort.

War powers resolutions rely on the War Powers Act, a Vietnam War-era law that allows Congress to compel the president to remove armed forces from unauthorized hostilities abroad. The Constitution grants Congress the power to declare war, though presidents have frequently deployed troops without formal declarations or legislative approval.

The vote occurred as the United States maintains a military presence in Lebanon without explicit congressional authorization for military operations there. Those supporting the resolution argued that the deployment went beyond presidential authority. Opponents contended that the military engagement served national security interests and did not require additional approval from lawmakers.

The rejection of the measure leaves current deployments in place unchanged. This marks another instance in which Congress has declined to exercise its war powers authority to restrict presidential military action. The Trump administration has not publicly responded to the vote.

The outcome reflects broader patterns in Congress regarding war powers oversight. While some lawmakers have pushed back against military deployments, particularly those without prior authorization or formal declarations, Republicans have largely declined to impose checks on Trump through war powers votes.

The debate over the Lebanon resolution fits into a wider conversation about presidential power and military intervention that has intensified during Trump's second term. Democrats have attempted to force votes on multiple war powers resolutions as the administration has increased military activities in various regions and discussed potential military operations elsewhere.

Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the Lebanon measure, seeking to constrain executive authority in the region. Democratic leaders in the House opposed the resolution despite it being sponsored by a member of their party, signaling internal disagreement about how aggressively to challenge Trump on foreign policy matters.

The war powers votes reflect longstanding constitutional tensions over who controls military decisions. The Framers intended Congress to declare war and authorize military force, but modern presidents across parties have increasingly asserted independent authority to deploy troops. Congressional efforts to reclaim this power through war powers resolutions have met with limited success, particularly when one party controls the chamber.

The failed Lebanon resolution suggests that reasserting congressional war powers authority remains difficult in the current political environment, despite growing concerns among some lawmakers about military expansion overseas.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens civil rights investigations into 15 medical schools
cards.teaser: The Civil Rights Division will examine whether the schools engaged in racial discrimination in admissions practices.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division has launched investigations into 15 medical schools over alleged racial discrimination in their admissions processes. The announcement comes after the DOJ recently found that medical schools at UCLA and Yale University illegally used race as a factor in admissions decisions.

The targeted schools all receive federal funding, which subjects them to civil rights laws prohibiting discrimination. These new investigations represent an expansion of the department's ongoing scrutiny into whether medical schools have engaged in race-conscious admissions practices.

cards.headline: House Oversight releases transcript of Bondi interview on Epstein files
cards.teaser: The former attorney general declined to answer multiple questions during the four-hour meeting.
cards.body:
The House Oversight and Government Reform Committee released the transcript from its closed-door meeting with former Attorney General Pam Bondi about her handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files. The transcript shows Bondi declining to answer a number of questions during the roughly four-hour meeting.

Bondi pointed to acting Attorney General Todd Blanche regarding questions about the files. The committee conducted the interview as part of its investigation into the handling of documents related to Epstein.

cards.headline: Man charged with threatening Senate Majority Leader John Thune
cards.teaser: An Oklahoma man faces federal charges for allegedly making death threats against the senator.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged an Oklahoma man with making death threats against Senate Majority Leader John Thune. The indictment describes the threats as retaliation for Thune's performance of his official duties.

The indictment does not allege a specific motive beyond the retaliation claim. Thune serves as the top Republican in the Senate.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. The former Interior Secretary served in the Biden administration before launching her gubernatorial campaign.

If elected in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor.

cards.headline: Trump proposes building pedestrian access at Lincoln Memorial
cards.teaser: The president said he wants to construct a pathway between the monument and the Potomac River.
cards.body:
President Trump said he wants to build pedestrian access between the Lincoln Memorial and the Potomac River. The proposal represents his latest plan to renovate prominent sites in Washington.

The project would add a pathway connecting the memorial to the river. Trump has proposed multiple changes to federal monuments and buildings in the capital during his presidency.

cards.headline: Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republicans and Democrats are selecting nominees to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
The California governor's race remains unsettled as election officials continue counting primary ballots, a process that could take days or weeks. Early results show British-born conservative Steve Hilton narrowly leading, with former US health and human services secretary Xavier Becerra in second place. Billionaire Tom Steyer trailed behind both candidates.

Under California's top-two primary system, the leading two vote-getters will advance to the general election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. All candidates compete on the same ballot regardless of party affiliation.
